rows.what: A Files & Docs tab lists the project's files together with the parent lead's files, guessing a folder for each lead file from its name.
rows.v2: Project › Files & notes › Files
rows.how: The project's Files are the lead's own Files — one set of files, not a merge — so nothing is guessed into a folder. Once the project is live, the lead's Files tab opens the project's.

rows.feature: Where you are in Files is in the address
rows.what: The tab is kept in the address, but the open folder, the grid or list view and an open preview are not.
rows.v2: Project › Files & notes › Files (?folder=…) and a file's own page
rows.how: The open folder is in the address and an open file has its own page, so Back and shared links land in the same place.

rows.feature: Ways into Files from the Overview
rows.what: The Overview's Key Files card (View all, Upload quote, Upload contract, Upload renders) switches to Files & Docs without opening a folder.
rows.v2: Project › Overview › Project info rows (Signed quote · Contract); Getting started › Contract; Project › Files & notes › Files
rows.how: The Overview has no Key Files card any more. The signed quote and the contract are Project info rows that open the record, the Contract step uploads the signed copy into Files, and Files is reached by its tab.

rows.what: Eight fixed folders — All Files, Contract/VO, Floor Plans, Renders, Quotes & BOQ, Site Photos, Variation Orders, From Qanvast — each with a file count.
rows.v2: Project › Files & notes › Files: Contract & VOs · Floor plans · Renders · Quotes & BOQ · Site photos, plus Payments · Site updates · Choices
rows.how: A new project opens with five starter folders the studio may rename, move or delete, and three system folders the project files into by itself. Variation orders share Contract & VOs; From Qanvast is not in the set (nothing filled it in 1.0).

rows.feature: Make, rename and delete your own folders
rows.what: The + button adds a folder, but it is not saved (gone after a reload); rename and delete work on desktop only, and deleting leaves the files under All Files.
rows.v2: Project › Files & notes › Files › New Folder; a folder's ⋮ › Rename · Move · Delete
rows.how: Folders are saved, can sit inside other folders, need a unique name and work on a phone too. Deleting a folder sends it and what is inside to the Trash, with Undo.

rows.what: A toggle switches between a list (the default) and a grid of cards.
rows.v2: Project › Files & notes › Files › View

rows.what: Upload sends the picked files one by one into the open folder (into Site Photos when All Files is open) and ends with one toast.
rows.v2: Project › Files & notes › Files › New File ▾ › From Local Files
rows.how: Files land in the open folder (the top level when none is open), never silently in Site photos. Each file has its own row in the upload toast while it uploads, with Retry if it fails.

rows.feature: Drag and drop files to upload
rows.what: Dropping files anywhere on the tab uploads them to the open folder.
rows.v2: Project › Files & notes › Files (drop on the page)

rows.what: The project's uploads have no size or type limit at all.
rows.v2: Project › Files & notes › Files › New File
rows.how: Any kind of file is kept, up to 8 MB each; a bigger file is refused with its name and the limit.

rows.what: The list shows Name, Type, Modified By (always "—") and Last Modified (really the upload time).
rows.v2: Project › Files & notes › Files › list (Column settings)
rows.how: Columns are Title · Owner · Updated · File type · File size · Attached to · Client, with the real owner and update time, and the shared Column settings drawer.

rows.what: Pictures show as thumbnails (the full-size original); other files show a tinted tile for PDF, spreadsheet or other.
rows.v1: Project › Files & Docs › list and grid
rows.v2: Project › Files & notes › Files
rows.how: A PDF shows its first page and a video its first frame; every other kind of work (sheet, deck, drawing, 3D model) has its own icon.

rows.what: A full-screen preview shows pictures only; any other file says "Preview unavailable · Download to open".
rows.v2: Project › Files & notes › Files › a file (its own page)
rows.how: The viewer opens pictures, PDFs and videos, zooms, steps with Previous / Next or ← / →, has a strip of the folder's files, and carries comments, information and Download.

rows.what: Download opens a one-hour signed link to the original file in a new tab.
rows.v2: Project › Files & notes › Files › ⋮ › Download; the viewer's Download

rows.what: Copy link puts an address on the clipboard, but no page exists behind it.
rows.v2: Project › Files & notes › Files › ⋮ › Copy link · Send on WhatsApp
rows.how: Copy link gives a signed, read-only link that really opens the file, and Send on WhatsApp drafts it to the client.

rows.feature: Show a file to the client
rows.what: A file's ⋯ menu shows it to the homeowner or hides it again (off by default); a HOMEOWNER pill marks it in the list, and an ⓘ explains the rule.
rows.v1: Project › Files & Docs › ⋯ › Show to homeowner / Hide from homeowner
rows.v2: Project › Files & notes › Files › ⋮ › Show to client / Stop showing to client; the Client column

rows.feature: What the client sees of the files
rows.what: The portal's Documents list every file shown to the homeowner, grouped by a category guessed from its name, plus signed quotes, the contract, receipts and selection receipts.
rows.v2: Portal › Files (the Files section switch on Company › Client portal)
rows.how: The client's Files list Documents by kind (Quotes · Agreements · Variation orders · Payment receipts · Selection receipts), then the files shown to them; the server checks every file against the portal's rules and section switches.

rows.what: Delete removes the file for good after a confirm, with no Undo; a lead's file deleted here is gone from the lead too.
rows.v2: Project › Files & notes › Files › ⋮ › Delete; ⋮ › Deleted Files
rows.how: Delete moves the file to the Trash with Undo; Deleted Files offers Restore, Delete forever and Empty. A file on a published update warns that the client sees it there.

rows.what: While the list loads, or when it fails, the tab shows "No files here yet" as if the project had none.
rows.v2: Project › Files & notes › Files
rows.how: The tab draws its own loading ghost, a real empty state and a no-results state, and a failed action says what failed.

rows.what: Activity shows "{name} uploaded {file} to {folder}" for the newest 30 uploads; deletes and shares leave no line.
rows.v2: Project › Files & notes › Activity (Files chip)
rows.how: Uploads, moves to the Trash, deletes for good, showing or hiding to the client, comments and the starter folders each leave a line naming who did it.

rows.feature: Documents the project files by itself
rows.what: Invoices file an empty entry with no file behind it, Visualizer and Co-Pilot renders file themselves, and the setup wizard files the contract under a folder name nothing else reads.
rows.v2: Project › Files & notes › Files › Payments · Site updates · Choices · Contract & VOs
rows.how: Receipts file into Payments, update media into Site updates, choice pictures into Choices, and the signed contract copy into Contract & VOs. Invoices stay on Money as pages of their own, not empty file rows.

rows.feature: Renders kept in the project's Files
rows.what: Every render variant made in the Visualizer for the project files itself into Renders as "Render - {room} - {style} - v{n}.png".
rows.v2: AI Visualizer › a version › Save to Files → Project › Files › Renders; Project › Design › Designs
rows.how: A render is filed only when someone presses Save to Files on a version (Renders is made on the first save); Designs lists the renders filed.

rows.feature: Co-Pilot renders and moodboards filed on the project
rows.what: A render or moodboard made in the meeting Co-Pilot for a project files itself into Renders.

rows.feature: Who may upload, delete or show a file
rows.what: Any signed-in member can upload, delete for good (lead files included) or show any file to the homeowner; the handover lock does not cover files.
rows.v2: Project › Files & notes › Files; Settings › Studio › Who may do what (Upload, rename, move and delete a lead’s or project’s files)
rows.how: Every file action is checked on the server against Who sees leads, and a project's money files are only for whoever sees its money. A completed project still leaves Files open, as 1.0 did.

rows.feature: Use a file from Files as a floor plan
rows.what: The project's Floor Plan offers to import a plan from a file already in Files & Docs.
rows.v2: Project › Design › Floor plan › ⋮ › Use a file from Files

rows.what: Files sit in a private storage bucket under studio/project/folder paths and open through one-hour signed links.
rows.v2: Project › Files & notes › Files (served by /files/raw and /files/thumb)
rows.how: The prototype keeps each file's bytes in its own database behind the same checks; developers put object storage behind these routes.

rows.what: A Quote tile shows the quote's line count and downloads its PDF, or lets you pick one (Signed · Draft · Upload) when there are several.
rows.v2: Project › Overview › Project info › Signed quote
rows.how: The Signed quote row opens the quote itself (preview and print) or the Won step's uploaded copy; there is no PDF picker, and a direct project lists its other quotes as rows.

rows.what: A Contract tile downloads the contract, or lets you pick among the project file, the lead's upload, an old link and the signed quote.
rows.v2: Project › Overview › Project info › Contract
rows.how: The Contract row opens the contract record ("Signed {date}") or the signed copy uploaded to Files; there is one contract to open, not a list of sources.

rows.feature: Key Files › Renders and the lightbox
rows.what: A Renders tile counts render files and update photos and opens a dark lightbox of the update photos (it opens nothing when only render files exist).
rows.v2: Project › Design › Designs (renders shared and filed); Project › Client › Updates (site photos)
rows.how: Renders and site photos are no longer mixed: renders sit in Designs, site photos in Updates and Files › Site updates.

rows.feature: Step through files: arrows and thumbnail strip
rows.what: The lightbox steps with ← / →, wraps around, has a thumbnail strip, opens PDFs, and offers Open in Files & Docs and Open in new tab.
rows.v2: Project › Files & notes › Files › a file (the viewer)
rows.how: The one file viewer has ← / →, a strip of the folder's files and PDF viewing; it is a page of its own, so "open in a new tab" is the browser's.

rows.what: The milestone drawer's "Related files" lists the invoices of that milestone with their status and opens a quick view of each.
rows.v1: Project › Management › Milestones › milestone drawer › Related files
rows.v2: Project › Schedule › a milestone's panel › Invoices
rows.how: The panel's Invoices rows (number, stage, amount, state) open on Money, and only for whoever sees the project's money.

rows.group: Contracts and quotes on a project
rows.what: A project takes one contract upload (up to 10 MB; PDF, Word, JPG or PNG) stored as its contract file.
rows.v1: Project › Draft setup › Contract; Key Files › Upload contract
rows.v2: Project › Overview › Getting started › Contract › Upload the signed copy (or link a signed contract)
rows.how: The Contract step links one of the client's contracts or uploads the signed copy into Files › Contract & VOs through the Files upload (8 MB).

rows.group: Contracts and quotes on a project
rows.feature: The signed contract reaches the project
rows.what: When the client signs, the signed PDF is written to every project of that lead that has no contract yet; a route can also build it from the lead's signature request.
rows.v2: Project › Overview › Project info › Contract
rows.how: The signed contract stays one record on the client's lead; the project reads it and shows "Signed {date}". No separate PDF copy is made.

rows.group: Contracts and quotes on a project
rows.feature: Contract value from quotes and variation orders
rows.what: The contract value is worked out on the server from the lead's or project's quotes plus approved variation orders, falling back to the project budget.
rows.v2: Project › Money; Projects listing › Contract value

rows.group: Contracts and quotes on a project
rows.feature: The schedule writes payment shares back to the quote
rows.what: Saving the timeline copies its payment milestones back into the contract quote, one way.
rows.v2: Project › Schedule (a milestone tied to a payment stage)
rows.how: The quote's Payment Schedule stays the source; a milestone can be tied to a stage, and nothing is written back into the quote.

rows.group: Contracts and quotes on a project
rows.feature: Variation orders as quotes of the project
rows.what: Variation orders are quotes of type variation tied to the project.
rows.v2: Project › Money › variation orders (the quote editor in variation mode)

rows.group: Contracts and quotes on a project
rows.feature: Turn a contractor's quote into a variation order
rows.what: The Quote Digitizer has a project picker beside the lead picker, to digitise a variation quote for a project.
rows.v2: Project › Money › New ▾ › Variation order from a contractor’s quote
rows.how: The upload is read on the project's Money tab and becomes a variation order to check in the editor.

rows.what: Roles are tags on a member — owner, admin, id (designer), accounting, manager — and a member may hold several.
rows.v2: Company › Members › Role
rows.how: Each member has one role: Owner, Admin, Manager or Designer. Only an Owner makes another Owner.

rows.what: Owners edit roles: name, colour, data scope (all · team · assigned), page access and action switches for leads, quotes, projects, tasks, finance, team and settings, and can add their own roles.
rows.how: Four fixed roles; a read-only Who may do what table on Settings › Studio lists every rule by role.

rows.what: A member can be given their own permission and workflow switches on top of their role.
An Accounting member sees only finance pages (landing on Finance › Pipeline), verifies payments and approves milestone-completion steps.
The manager tag is a lead hierarchy for one studio only; no project code reads it.
rows.v2: Company › Members (Manager role and reports-to)
rows.how: A Manager sees and changes their team's projects, and sees the Workload view for their team.

rows.what: Designers see only projects they are assigned to, but the filter runs in the browser — the server returns every project and opens any project by its address.
rows.v2: Settings › Lead management › Who sees leads (a project follows its lead)
rows.how: Who sees a project follows who sees its lead (Everyone, or Only the leads assigned to them; Managers see their team's), checked on the server on every page, action and task.

rows.what: Seeded roles let Owners and Admins create projects, but nothing checks it — New Project shows for everyone.
rows.v2: Projects › New project (C)

rows.what: The edit permission only hides the Team card; every project route accepts any signed-in member.
rows.v2: Project page (every change); Settings › Studio › Who may do what
rows.how: Only the project's team, their Managers, Owners and Admins change a project, and the server refuses anyone else with that sentence.

rows.feature: Who may change a project's team
rows.what: Any member can add or remove assignees and change their commission split; the split is not checked.
rows.v2: Project › info column › Members; Company › Finance › Commission › Commission shares
rows.how: A project's members are its lead's members, changed with the same reach as a lead's; commission shares are set by Owners and Admins in Finance and always add up to 100%.

rows.what: Owners and Admins delete a project for good, unless it has any financial activity.
rows.v2: Project › ⋮ › Delete; Projects › ⋮ › Deleted Projects
rows.how: Still Owners and Admins, but a delete is soft (Restore, Delete forever) and is refused only while payments are recorded or invoices have gone to the client.

rows.what: Only members with the payment-schedule override (Owners and Admins) may change a payment schedule once it is frozen on a project or a quote.
rows.v1: Project › Finance › payment schedule; a quote's payment schedule
rows.v2: Settings › Quotes & pricing › Payment schedule (keep it to Owners and Admins)
rows.how: A studio switch decides whether only Owners and Admins change a quote's payment schedule; a project with a signed quote takes its split from that quote, and a direct project's split is changed by its team until a stage's invoice has gone out.

rows.what: Owners and Admins archive a project (its open tasks are cancelled) and unarchive it.

rows.feature: Approve or reject a project's closure
rows.what: Only an Owner sees Approve / Reject on a closure in the browser; the server lets any member approve or reject, even when nothing was submitted.
rows.v2: Project › Overview › Hand over (review); Settings › Projects › What waits for an Owner or an Admin › Handover needs an owner’s review
rows.how: Owners and Admins approve or send back a handover, checked on the server; the review is a setting, off by default.

rows.what: Only an Owner sees the listing's Table / Workload toggle and the portfolio tiles with Total Pipeline.
rows.v2: Projects › Workload view; Projects listing tiles; Company › Reports › Projects
rows.how: The Workload view is for Owners, Admins and Managers (their team); the listing's money is for Owners and Admins.

rows.what: Only an Owner sets a custom commission rate when creating a project; anyone else's rate becomes a change request.
rows.v2: Settings › Finance › Commission; Company › Finance › Commission (ask for another rate)
rows.how: Owners and Admins set rates; a member asks for another rate on a project they work on, and the ask is answered in Finance.

rows.feature: Asking for more time on a milestone
rows.what: A non-owner asks for a later end date with a reason, which waits for the owner; an owner moves the date directly.
rows.v2: Project › Schedule › a milestone's panel › Ask for more time

rows.what: Owners, Admins and Accounting verify a payment on the project's Finance tab.
rows.v2: Settings › Finance › Client payments (who confirms); Project › Money
rows.how: A payment the studio records is confirmed as it is entered; a client's "I have paid" waits for the confirmer the studio names (the project's designer by default) or any Owner or Admin.

rows.what: Owners always approve held progress updates, plus the members on the approvers list; the later approve / reject call is not checked.
rows.v2: Settings › Projects › What waits for an Owner or an Admin › Updates (Who reviews)

rows.what: Each workflow (quote, timeline, milestone, PO, expense, commission, price book) has its own list of extra approvers beside the Owners.
rows.v2: Settings › Projects › What waits for an Owner or an Admin (Who approves)
rows.how: Owners and Admins approve every project and money approval; only updates have named reviewers, and quotes keep one backup approver.

rows.what: Finance Operations, Pipeline, Reports and Vendors are for Owners, Admins and Accounting; Designers reach only the Finance overview and Commissions.
rows.v2: Company › Finance (To do · Money out · Vendors · My commission · Xero)
rows.how: Every member opens Company › Finance and sees the money of the projects they work on; Xero and the finance reports are for Owners and Admins.

rows.what: The role editor shows View invoices, Create invoices, Record payments, Manage POs, Manage expenses, Approve expenses and View reports, but nothing applies them.
rows.v2: Settings › Studio › Who may do what › Money in · Money out · Profit and commission
rows.how: Each money action has one fixed rule, checked on the server and listed in Who may do what.

rows.what: The project's Finance tab and the money routes behind it show invoices, payments, costs and commission rules to any member.
rows.v2: Project › Money (Settings › Studio › Who may do what › See a project’s money)
rows.how: The contract value, invoices and payments are for the project's team, their Managers, Owners and Admins, checked on the server; its money files in Files are hidden from anyone else.

rows.what: Margins and profit show on the project's Finance tab and the closure summary to anyone who opens them.
rows.v2: Project › Overview › Money; Company › Reports › Finance
rows.how: Profit, margin and cost totals are for Owners and Admins only.

rows.what: Designers can raise milestone invoices from the Gantt; an approval gate holds them only when the studio asks.
rows.v2: Project › Money; Settings › Projects › What waits for an Owner or an Admin › Invoices need approval
rows.how: The project's team prepares invoices; with Invoices need approval on (the default) a Designer's or a Manager's waits for an Owner or an Admin.

rows.feature: Who may use the vendor directory
rows.what: A designer may add a vendor while making a PO or expense, but may not open, correct or merge the directory.
rows.v2: Company › Finance › Vendors
rows.how: Every member adds a vendor and opens Vendors; changing, deactivating or merging a vendor and seeing its bank details is for Owners and Admins.

rows.what: Designers submit expenses; Owners, Admins and Accounting approve them.
rows.v2: Company › Finance › Money out › Expenses; Company › Finance › To do

rows.feature: See the portal as the client
rows.what: Any member can open a 30-minute read-only preview of the homeowner's portal.
rows.v2: Invite to Portal panel › See it as {client}
rows.how: Whoever works on the lead (its members, their Manager, Owners and Admins) opens the client's real pages read-only in a new tab.

rows.what: Only archive, unarchive and delete check a role on the server; every other rule lives in the browser.
rows.v2: Every project and money action (server actions)
rows.how: Every project, file and money action checks the viewer's role and reach on the server and refuses with the rule in words.

rows.feature: Who may change the studio's settings
rows.what: Any member who reaches Accounts Setup can change most tabs; only the Roles editor is Owner-only.
rows.v2: Settings (every module)
rows.how: Owners and Admins change Settings; everyone else reads it in a read-only look.

rows.what: A switch (on by default) holds a non-approver's progress update for review before the homeowner sees it.
rows.v2: Settings › Projects › What waits for an Owner or an Admin › Updates
rows.how: Same rule, now with the other project approvals on Settings › Projects.

rows.what: A switch said project timelines need an owner's approval before going live; the workflow behind it was removed, so it did nothing.
rows.v2: Settings › Projects › What waits for an Owner or an Admin › Schedule changes need approval before the client sees them
rows.how: A real switch now: a Designer's or a Manager's share of schedule changes waits for an Owner or an Admin (off by default).

rows.what: A switch makes an owner approve the tasks generated for a milestone, and also holds milestone invoices for approval.
rows.v2: Settings › Projects › What waits for an Owner or an Admin › Milestone completion needs approval · Invoices need approval
rows.how: Two separate switches: a non-owner's Done on a milestone waits (off by default), and invoices have their own approval. AI-generated milestone tasks are not built.

rows.feature: Contract and project type required; setup gates
rows.what: Workflow switches require a signed contract and a project type before a lead is Signed, and a Draft project turns Active by itself once assignment, quote, contract, timeline and commission are done.
rows.v1: Accounts › Workflow Rules; project Draft setup
rows.v2: Lead › Move stage › Won; Project › Overview › Getting started › Start the project
rows.how: The Won step always asks for the quote, the contract, a payment split of 100% and the project type — no switches. The project then waits in Setting up with a Getting started card until the team presses Start the project; nothing flips the stage by itself.

rows.what: A switch sends POs to accounting review, with a PO review threshold and an advance payment review threshold.
rows.v1: Accounts › Workflow Rules; Accounts › Finance › PO Settings
rows.v2: Settings › Finance › Costs (Approval limit, who approves)
rows.how: POs over the limit or with an advance need an Owner's or an Admin's approval (on, S$5,000 by default).

rows.what: A switch makes a designer's expenses wait for approval.
rows.v2: Settings › Finance › Costs
rows.how: The same switch (on by default), now beside the other cost rules; Owners and Admins approve.

rows.what: A switch turns commission off for every project and skips the commission step on new ones.
rows.v2: Settings › Finance › Commission (the studio's rule: No commission)
rows.how: Picking No commission as the studio's rule turns commission off; there is no separate switch.

rows.what: A switch makes an Owner or Admin approve invoices before they reach the homeowner.
rows.v1: Accounts › Finance › PO Settings › Invoice Approval
rows.v2: Settings › Projects › What waits for an Owner or an Admin › Invoices need approval before they’re sent
rows.how: The same switch (on by default), now with the other project approvals.

rows.what: A feature flag (off by default) locks a closed project's milestones, updates and details for everyone but Owners and Admins, in the browser only.
rows.v2: Project (Completed) › ⋮ › Reopen
rows.how: Always on and checked on the server: a completed project's schedule and money are read-only for everyone until an Owner or an Admin reopens it; recording a payment stays open.

rows.what: A feature flag adds a CaseTrust deposit-protection disclosure to the client's signing page (Singapore only).
rows.v2: Company › Profile › Registrations & accreditations (CaseTrust)
rows.how: Being CaseTrust-accredited on the studio's one record of registrations turns the disclosure and its tick on.

rows.feature: Proactive alerts before a milestone is due
rows.what: When on, each milestone due within the lead time (1–30 days, 7 by default) gets a review task for the owner.
rows.v2: Settings › Projects › Schedule › Alerts lead time
rows.how: The lead time (1–30 days, 3 by default) raises bell rows for the team when a milestone ends soon or a project task is due, not tasks for the owner; there is no master switch.

rows.what: Two switches: notify the owner of a designer's extension request (an approval task) and log a progress update when one is asked.
rows.v1: Accounts › Workflow › Proactive Alerts › Extension Request Settings
rows.v2: Project › Schedule › a milestone's panel (Ask for more time); Overview › Needs your OK
rows.how: An ask always reaches Owners and Admins (the bell and Needs your OK); approving can draft an update, chosen per answer, not by a setting.

rows.what: The studio keeps its own list of project types.
rows.how: Three fixed types: Whole-home renovation · Partial renovation · Commercial fit-out.

rows.feature: Project & Payments: templates per project type
rows.what: Each project type carries milestone templates with offsets, payment %, due criteria, notes to the homeowner and designer payout rules.
rows.v2: Company › Templates › Schedules; Company › Templates › Payment schedules; Settings › Finance › Commission
rows.how: Schedules, payment splits and commission are three libraries of their own; there are no per-type payout rules.

rows.what: For each project type, a default list of milestones (name, days, colour) that the Gantt's "Reset to template" reads, with reorder and reset.
rows.v2: Settings › Projects › Schedule › Where a schedule starts, by project type; Company › Templates › Schedules
rows.how: Each of the three project types (and the studio default) picks a schedule template, including five ready-made ones.

rows.what: A page lists the timelines saved from a Gantt, to rename or delete them.
rows.v2: Company › Templates › Schedules
rows.how: The one Schedules library holds them, with folders, rename and delete.

rows.what: The studio edits the categories used for escalation tickets.
rows.v2: Settings › Projects › Ticket categories
rows.how: The same editable list, named for tickets, beside the other project rules.

rows.what: The studio's reusable materials: browse, add, edit, archive, vendor and image.
rows.v2: Company › Materials
rows.how: The same catalogue as a Company library; choices pick options from it.

rows.what: The studio sets the invoice, PO and ticket prefixes, with numbering per issuing company; projects have no number pattern (shown as #N).
rows.v2: Settings › Finance › Document numbers; Settings › Projects › Project numbers
rows.how: Invoices, receipts, credit notes and POs take full patterns (with an invoice prefix per issuing entity) and projects get their own number. The ticket prefix is fixed (T-{year}-…) and cannot be changed.

rows.what: The studio's payment schedule templates and its default.
rows.v2: Company › Templates › Payment schedules
rows.how: The same templates in the Templates library, with folders and a default.

rows.what: Bank details, PayNow or DuitNow ID, an uploaded QR, who confirms a homeowner's payment and whether a homeowner's upload is trusted at once.
rows.v2: Company › Profile › Issuing entities & bank details; Settings › Finance › Client payments
rows.how: Bank, PayNow and the QR sit on each issuing entity (the uploaded QR is a stand-in picture in the prototype); the confirmer and the trust switch are on Client payments. DuitNow went with other countries.

rows.what: The studio edits its expense categories, each marked overhead or not.
rows.v2: Company › Finance › Money out › Expenses (category)
rows.how: A fixed list of eleven categories; overhead is chosen on each expense (Studio overhead).

rows.what: A studio default rate on revenue or profit, overrides per designer, per project and per designer on a project, accrued per milestone payment or once per project.
rows.v2: Settings › Finance › Commission
rows.how: Rates by studio, member, project and member-on-project: % of what the client pays, % of the profit, a fixed amount per project, or none; a change applies from its day.

rows.what: Connect Xero, map accounts and tax codes, backfill, push invoices, payments, bills and credit notes, with a sync log and Retry.
rows.v2: Company › Integrations (Xero); Company › Finance › Xero
rows.how: The screens, mapping, pushes and log are built, but nothing talks to Xero; developers wire the real connection.

rows.what: Per document type, a studio default and a per-company override: header and footer notes, terms blocks, bank details and balance due switches, an accent colour and a live preview.
rows.v2: Settings › Finance › Invoice paper
rows.how: Invoices, receipts and variation orders print the studio's paper (notes, terms, bank and balance switches) with an override per issuing entity; colours come from the brand kit and a variation order also prints through the quote templates.

rows.what: The studio's companies with their tax and bank details, used on invoices and the payment portal.
rows.v2: Company › Profile › Issuing entities & bank details
rows.how: Each issuing entity keeps its bank, PayNow and letterhead; a project's invoices take the signed quote's entity.

rows.what: Owners switch in-app, email and WhatsApp per category (Projects, Invoices, Purchase Orders, Finance Operations, Tasks & Escalations …).
rows.v2: Settings › Notifications › Events and channels
rows.how: Channels are switched per event (each project and money event its own row) rather than per category; Owners and Admins change them and everyone else reads them.

rows.what: A Digest box per category collects non-urgent emails into one daily email.
A Recipients popover per category picks which roles hear it.
rows.how: Who hears each event is fixed by the event (the Who column on Settings › Notifications).

rows.what: Switches for the emails sent to clients: a signing confirmation and a payment confirmation (and a Hangout meeting notice).
rows.v2: Settings › Notifications › Messages to clients
rows.how: Twelve client messages (invoice sent, payment due, payment confirmed, something to sign or approve, schedule shared, update, issue answered, message, choice, paused, resumed, handed over) by email and WhatsApp in the studio's words. No message confirms a signature to the client.

rows.what: Studios edit each notification's wording with variables, a preview and Reset.
rows.v2: Settings › Notifications › Messages

rows.what: The dispatcher emails and sends WhatsApp templates through 360dialog for each event.
rows.v2: Settings › Notifications › Sent messages
rows.how: Every email and WhatsApp is composed and logged in Sent messages, but none leaves; developers plug in a provider.

rows.feature: Make a project from a lead
rows.what: Once the studio's prerequisites pass, the lead drawer offers Create Project, which opens a create drawer.
rows.v2: Lead › Move stage › Won (creates the project)
rows.how: Won creates the project at once; a Getting started card replaces the drawer and the Draft wizard.

rows.what: A project made without a lead quietly makes one, parked at a closed stage so it never shows in the pipeline.
rows.v2: Projects › New project

rows.feature: What a project takes from its lead
rows.what: At creation the project copies the lead's phone, email, property type and address, project type, issuing entity and the quote's payment schedule.
rows.v2: Project › info column (the lead's own fields)
rows.how: Nothing is copied: the client and property stay on the lead and the project reads them, so one edit shows on both.

rows.feature: Open the project from its lead
rows.what: The lead drawer shows View Project, and a "commission pending" hint while the project is still a Draft.
rows.v2: Lead › header › Open P-…; the lead's tabs
rows.how: The lead's header opens the project, and once it is live the lead's Tasks, Files, Notes & Logs, Questionnaire and Activity open the project's.

rows.what: Creating a second project for a lead is refused ("A project already exists for this lead").
rows.v2: Lead › Won; Leads › Delete (refused while a project exists)

rows.feature: Team and phone changes reach the project
rows.what: Changing a lead's assignees updates its project's team, and a new phone is pushed to every project of the lead.
rows.v2: Lead / Project › Members; Edit details
rows.how: There is nothing to sync: the project's members and phone are the lead's own.

rows.feature: Project tasks on the Tasks page
rows.what: The Tasks page filters All · Leads · Projects, groups by project with Go to project, and opens approval tasks on the right project tab.
rows.v2: Tasks › All · Leads · Projects; ⋮ › Group by project

rows.what: Progress review, closure, commission, invoice review and milestone approval reach people as tasks; approving the task approves the record.
rows.v2: Project › Overview › Needs your OK; the bell; Projects › Needs my review
rows.how: An approval is a state on the record with a bell row; the approver acts on the record itself, not on a task.

rows.what: A chat can carry a project, shown in the inbox list, header and side panel with Go to Project.
rows.v2: Messages (rail) › a conversation › Open project; Project › Client › Messages
rows.how: Every conversation belongs to a project and opens on its Messages view.

rows.what: An escalation can be tied to a project; open ones lower its health and appear in its action items.
rows.v2: Project › Client › Tickets; Projects › Needs attention
rows.how: Escalated tickets and tickets waiting on the studio raise the project in Needs attention.

rows.what: The home shows a project count, an owner-only feed of recent updates, margin and compliance alerts linking into projects, and a Site Update chip.
Finance Pipeline lists projects with their contract values, and Operations works project by project.
rows.v2: Company › Finance (To do · Money out); Company › Reports › Finance
rows.how: Finance is a Company section and every report is in Company › Reports; each money row names its project.

rows.feature: Open the AI Visualizer for a project
rows.what: The Visualizer opens bound to the project; its rooms and renders carry the project.
rows.v1: Project › Photo Renders → Tools › AI Visualizer
rows.v2: Project › ⋮ › Open in AI Visualizer
rows.how: It opens the lead's design and Back returns to the project.

rows.feature: Floor Plan tool for a project
rows.what: The Floor Plan tool, opened with a project, lists that project's saved plans.
rows.v2: Project › Design › Floor plan; 3-D Space Planner layouts on the project
rows.how: Plans live on the project itself.

rows.what: An Owner-only directory of clients from projects and leads: edit a client's contact, family members per project, and preview as homeowner.
rows.v2: Company › Client portal › Clients; Invite to Portal panel
rows.how: Owners and Admins change the portal's set-up; whoever works on a lead invites, withdraws and sees it as the client; the household replaces family members.

rows.what: Co-Pilot sessions and meeting briefs carry the project, and the project page has a Meeting Summary card.
rows.v1: Tools › Meeting Co-Pilot; Project › Overview › Meeting Summary

rows.what: The mAIson bot can list, create and update projects, draft a plan, read a project's money, raise milestone invoices and create tasks (Owners, Admins and Designers).
rows.v2: Maison AI on a project page
rows.how: Maison AI on a project answers (what is overdue), proposes a task or an update and adds it on confirm, within the viewer's own rules; it does not create projects or raise invoices, and AI-written plans are held.

rows.what: Search matches projects on name, client, phone, address, project type and assignee name, from data already loaded in the browser.
rows.v2: ⌘K search › Projects
rows.how: Server-side, Who sees leads applied: projects match on name, number, client, phone, property, type and household, and invoice, receipt, credit note and ticket numbers find their project. A member's name does not find their projects.

rows.what: The Projects item's badge counts projects whose old status is Planning, Hacking or In Progress (closed ones keep counting).
rows.v2: Rail › Projects
rows.how: The badge counts projects that need attention and opens that list.

rows.what: The quick-action menu's New Project, Create Quote and Upload File all just open Projects.
rows.v2: ⌘K › Create (New project, Create quote, New task …); key C
rows.how: Each Create entry opens the real form; there is no separate Upload File entry.

rows.what: A project's country sets currency, tax, phone rules, compliance lists and floor-plan templates, and locks once invoiced.

rows.feature: A record of edits to a project
rows.what: Field edits, stage changes, archive, delete and team changes leave no trace.
rows.v2: Project › Files & notes › Activity
rows.how: Edits, team changes, holds, the ending and deletes are logged with who did them and show in Activity.

new_in_2.feature: Rename, move, duplicate, select many, search and filter files
new_in_2.note: 1.0's tab had none of these; one bulk bar does Move to Folder · Duplicate · Delete.

new_in_2.v2: Project › Files & notes › Files › a file › Comments
new_in_2.note: Members comment on a file; the bell tells the file's people.
Restore, Delete forever and Empty; 1.0 deleted for good.
Says whether a task, a note or a return holds the file.

new_in_2.feature: Money files kept from members who don't see money
new_in_2.note: A client's proof, receipts and invoices in Files follow the money rule (F-17).

new_in_2.v2: Settings › Studio › Who may do what
new_in_2.note: Read-only table of every rule by role, grouped by area, built from the same functions the server checks.
Twelve automatic client emails / WhatsApps in the studio's words, each with its own switch.
Every email and WhatsApp the studio sent; Owners and Admins see all, others their own.

new_in_2.v2: Projects › ⋮ › Export all as… ; bulk bar › Export

new_in_2.feature: Project capacity per member and the Workload view
new_in_2.v2: Company › Members; Projects › ?view=workload; Settings › Projects › Workload
new_in_2.note: Capacity 1–20 per member with a studio default.
HDB BTO, HDB resale, Condo, Landed, Commercial fit-out.
A prefix / year / digits pattern; 1.0 showed a bare #N.

notes: Renders in the Visualizer, shared-render feedback and selection receipts were left to the tasks reader as instructed, and the notification events and crons to the updates reader; only their settings and the files they leave on a project are mapped here. 1.0's file Approve / Reject (REVIEW, APPROVED, SHARED and APPROVAL REQUESTED pills, the Variation Orders red dot) was skipped: nothing in 1.0 ever set a file to pending, so no studio could reach it. Platform-only switches (the Qanvast admin's page switches and notification pause, Studio Health, analytics events, the unused offline queue and project_templates) were not mapped. Not verified: whether 2.0 refuses changing a lead's issuing entity once its project exists (1.0's count-by-lead lock, J-80, J-211) — each 2.0 invoice takes the signed quote's entity — and the exact Commission payout timing against 1.0's 'once at closure' mode. Several money settings (Payment Methods, Commission, Expense categories, PO Settings, Xero, invoice paper) are mapped here as settings and may also appear in the money reader's rows.
